## Objective
- Build a complete, playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each new case randomizes a victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a definitive smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Gameplay stages: 2:00 AM phone call, top-down scene with four inspectable objects, close-up clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, and win/loss screens.
- Accusing incorrectly or accusing before finding the smoking gun loses; correctly accusing after finding it wins.
- Designed for vertical mobile with no scrolling.

## Decisions
- Built from scratch as a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Added optional user-enabled synthesized rain/phone audio; no external runtime dependencies.

## Work State

### Completed
- Implemented randomized cases, four interactive objects/clues, evidence board, suspect accusation flow, and victory/game-over logic.
- Built noir office, crime-scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views with mobile-focused styling.
- Tested several screens using mobile-sized Playwright screenshots; fixed a win-screen null-reference issue and refined layouts.
- Added booking/last-known portrait card to the end screen in the latest changes.

### Active
- Validate the latest end-screen portrait changes and retest full game flow, including correct accusation with smoking gun and incorrect accusation / missing smoking gun.
- Check responsive no-scroll layout and JavaScript syntax after the latest edits.

1. Run `node --check game.js` and inspect the latest changes for runtime errors.
2. Use a mobile viewport to verify end screens and both win/loss paths, plus board/scene layout.
3. Fix any issues found; summarize assumptions and checks when finishing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens, scene/object markup, evidence board, accusation and end-screen structure.
- `game.js`: Case generation, clues, state, rendering, game flow, optional sound, and end-screen behavior.
- `styles.css`: Noir visuals, animations, and vertical mobile layouts.
- `fonts/`: Locally bundled fonts used by the game.
